raw_request: Remove the old dsh-tui design and implementation, restart from scratch, and establish the new design using AppSDK governance.
understood_objective: Create a fresh AppSDK-governed design for a TypeScript/Node Cordis TUI that leaves the official DSH WebUI unchanged, connects as an independent client to the same official ApiProxy and ACP Session truth, defaults to a new current-cwd session, supports current-cwd resume through --resume or /resume, independently aligns presentation behavior to official WebUI source and tests, and implements every presentation and terminal control as a grouped Cordis plugin.
acceptance_criteria: The legacy dsh-tui tree and TUI-only worktrees are absent from the workspace, with committed history recoverable from Git and the old main tree retained in a trash backup.
The dsh-tui project is initialized by external AppSDK 0.1.3, the SDK lock is pinned, and appsdk verify passes.
The official DSH Web profile and official WebUI packages are neither modified nor replaced.
The architecture has one official DSH Host truth and two clients: official WebUI and independent terminal TUI.
The TUI profile is client-only and never mounts dsh-base, Agent, Session persistence, model adapters, or a second inference Host.
The TUI defaults to session.create with the canonical current cwd; --resume and /resume accept only sessions whose canonical cwd equals the current cwd.
Transport uses public DSH HTTP, WebSocket, schema, and generic RPC contracts; no private DSH src import is permitted.
TUI presentation plugins independently implement behavior extracted from official WebUI source and tests; official WebUI and TUI do not share presentation runtime code.
Terminal renderers consume typed TUI presentation nodes and never consume raw Session events, pair tool calls, or infer control state.
Every component is a Cordis plugin registered into typed grouped registries, and a static Web simulator renders the TUI canonical model for visual approval.
No runtime implementation begins until the AppSDK maps, capability bindings, Codex TUI selection audit, public-input audit, and verification gates are admitted.
non_goals: Modify the official Web profile or replace official WebUI presentation plugins.
Share presentation implementation between official WebUI and TUI.
Use Rust or a Node-to-Rust bridge.
Provide general multi-session, cross-workspace resume, or Session management screens.
Read DSH persistence files directly or create a second Session/Agent truth.
Implement runtime code during this design-reset change.
assumptions: The official DSH Web host is already running on an explicit loopback endpoint when the TUI starts.
The public DSH Session/API/event/projection/tool-view/generic-RPC contracts are the only runtime integration boundary.
Official WebUI source and tests are reference evidence only and are absent from the installed TUI dependency graph.
A capability whose required business data is not publicly observable is marked individually blocked and cannot use a private import, copied runtime dependency, or fallback.
ambiguities: The exact TypeScript terminal rendering library and component lifecycle remain pending the required audit of ~/code/codex.
Each official WebUI semantic capability still requires a source-to-public-input audit before its binding can be admitted.
